note: Real screenshots of the SetuHQ site as built in site/. Nothing is drawn or edited.
rule: window 1440x900 CSS px at device scale 2, reduced motion; frame 1360x850 CSS px of the content column (x 40), starting 32 px above the anchor element (a Methods stage, or the heading before it), never above the end of the block before; top bar and page bar hidden

shots.alt: Mission Control: the catalogue line (8,376 planets and 5,684 stars from exoplanet.eu, fetched 2026-10-18; 8,049 planets placed; the run tess-pi-men-s1 with 7 dips; the feed's 24 entries), the sweep line (200 stars, 936 dips reviewed, 1,011 entries by class) and the linked panes: the Galaxy with pi Men selected and its three planets, the sky position and the stored light curve with its dips. Selecting a star in one pane selects it in every pane.

The home page's hero, The sky, reviewed.: SetuHQ searches any TESS star's public light curve for transits; a calibrated panel of Sentinels (AI reviewers) and Probes (deterministic detectors) marks the dips, and vetting explains every verdict; nothing is called a planet until it is one. Beside it, on a black stage, a model from stored values: pi Men (5,992 K and 1.15 solar radii, TESS Input Catalog v8.2) in its blackbody colour, crossed by pi Men c at Rp/R★ 0.0150 (exoplanet.eu's radius over the stored stellar radius), and the light curve that crossing makes, depth 245 ppm over 3.20 hours; the planet is tagged an artist's impression. A Pause button stops the loop.

Worked examples on the home page: five cards, one per stored run on public TESS light curves, each with a black stage (a model from stored values: the star's disc in its blackbody colour at its stored Teff, and what the run measured as shadows at its fitted Rp/R★), then the kind of example, the star, a one-line summary, its dips counted by vetting outcome, its sector and panel, and links to its case file, plates and run report. WASP-126, hot Jupiter, 5,676 K: 8 dips (8 candidates), Probes only; TOI-270, multi-planet system, 3,532 K: 7 dips (5 candidates, 2 flagged), b drawn dashed as not recovered, Probes only; HD 15337, small planets near the limit, 5,175 K: 3 dips (2 candidates, 1 flagged), Probes only; TOI-236, known false positive, 6,422 K: an occulter not identified, secondary eclipse at SNR 10.9, 6 dips (6 rejected), Probes only; pi Men, reference check, 5,992 K: 7 dips (5 candidates, 1 flagged, 1 rejected), Probes and Sentinels.

Galaxy: every known exoplanet, around the Sun. 8,049 planets around 5,433 stars placed where exoplanet.eu lists them, in 3D galactic coordinates, with distance rings in light-years, a radar and a heads-up readout of the planets near the aim. The app states that it maps these planets and did not find them.
Catalogue: all 8,376 exoplanet.eu records in a sortable, filterable table with text search and CSV export, each row linking to the planet's own page.

A planet page, pi Men c (transit, discovered 2018, super-Earth): an artist's impression chosen from its measured radius and computed irradiation (1.87 Earth radii, so drawn with a gaseous envelope; Teq 1,179 K from a, the star's radius and Teff, the hot band; composition not measured; exoplanet.eu, fetched 2026-10-18), labelled as one, with a Spin button, beside its star pi Men drawn in its blackbody colour at 6,037 K, a model from stored values.

Transit case for the dip at BTJD 1331.77 on pi Men c, a known planet: 241 ppm, 2.46 hours, SNR 16.0, candidate, unconfirmed. The seven dips of the run as tabs (coloured by vetting status), the transit played back from stored values (star and planet to scale, the orbit not), and who marked it: 5 of 5 reviewers, two Sentinels and three Probes, each with its calibrated weight, around the stored panel score of 1.00.

Methods, chapter 4 of 15, Radial velocity: 51 Peg b and its star orbiting their shared centre of mass, with the radial-velocity curve (K = 56.7 m/s from m sin i; stored 55.77 m/s) and the star's spectral lines shifting; labelled a model from stored values, the star's motion exaggerated 1,000 times.

Methods, chapter 11 of 15, Reading atmospheres: A real spectrum, WASP-39 b with JWST. The NIRSpec PRISM transmission spectrum (Carter et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0), 36 binned points with error bars and the paper's best-fit model, transit depth from 20,607 to 23,063 ppm over 0.5 to 5.5 µm, with Na, K, H₂O, CH₄, CO₂ and CO bands marked; the deepest point is at 4.37 µm, the carbon dioxide band. Labelled real data, cited.

Methods, chapter 7 of 15, Blocking starlight: a Lyot coronagraph computed with Fraunhofer optics in four planes (the entrance pupil, the focal plane with a 4 λ/D occulting disc, the Lyot plane with the stop at 80% of the pupil, the final image) and the starlight's log-intensity profile out to 12 λ/D: at 8 λ/D it is 1.8×10⁻⁷ of the star's peak, against 7.8×10⁻⁵ with no coronagraph. Labelled an illustration: ideal monochromatic optics, a log stretch, the planet at an illustrative 10⁻³.
